Subject: Security questionnaire + dataflow artifacts for DPA review

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and DPA review, our privacy team has a short security questionnaire focused on PII handling, model telemetry, and credentialing for any connectors/subprocessors that touch telemetry. Can you confirm the following and share artifacts where possible?

1) A dataflow diagram that shows telemetry paths from ingestion to short-term cache and long-term observability stores (indicate where PII is filtered/pseudonymized).
2) A short description of credentialing/role-based access for pods that process user inputs, including who holds KMS keys and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed.
3) List of subprocessors that may see raw telemetry and the contractual attestation for each (SOC2 / SSAE / equivalent).
4) Retention windows for token-level telemetry used for model performance vs. audit logs.
5) Any cross-border transfer controls we should include in the DPA annex.

We're trying to keep the loop tight: target response by EOD Tuesday so our legal/privacy teams can finalize the DPA annex. I've attached the SSQ template from our side for reference (ssq_medtech_v1.xlsx) and flagged the must-have items.

Thanks,
Aisha

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear ask and the template.

Quick plan and what I'll attach:
- redwood_dataflow_v2.svg (attached) — visual showing ingress, short-lived KV cache, batching layer, model serving, and telemetry exporter. I annotated PII-filtering points (ingest predicates + tokenizer-level redaction).
- provisional subprocessor roster + attestation references (I will include SOC/ISO references next email).
- short write-up on credentialing, KMS custody and key-splitting approach.

Answers at a glance:
- Credentialing: access to production inference pools is gated by SSO + MFA + Just-in-Time role elevation with 4-eyes for key unwrap events. Pod-level service identities are issued short-lived certs via our internal CA; all operator actions are logged to an immutable audit stream.
- KMS: by default Redwood-managed keys live in our cloud KMS (multi-tenant) but we offer customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated/Private customers. For telemetry used in diagnostics we recommend customer-managed keys for regulated accounts.
- Subprocessors: the inference runtime calls a small set of managed services (metrics/observability, SSO provider, storage). I'll attach the current roster and the compliance snapshot (SOC2 Type II dates).
- Retention: token-level telemetry for modeling/perf is kept 30 days by default (configurable down to 0); aggregated model metrics retained for 2 years; immutable audit logs retained per contract (default 1 year).
- Cross-border: we support region pinning; telemetry egress can be restricted to a region and we provide a transfer annex with subprocessors and SCCs where applicable.

I'll loop Marissa for the SSQ matrix (she's preparing the itemized responses) and Connor for the artifact packaging (audit logs + SOC references). Expect the draft response and attachments within 24 hours.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire + dataflow artifacts for DPA review

Hi Aisha — attaching the draft SSQ response (ssq_response_draft.docx) and summarizing key answers inline below for quick review. Please tell us if you want the answers moved into your spreadsheet or prefer we populate both.

Excerpted answers (high level):
1) Dataflow and PII handling:
   - Ingest: customer frontends push requests into an ingress API layer. The ingress applies request predicates and tokenizers; configured rules redacting common PII patterns (PII regex + ML-based detectors) before payloads reach persistent storage.
   - KV Cache: ephemeral per-session KV cache (TTL default 5 minutes) used to accelerate autoregressive decoding. The cache resides on the serving node and is not written to long-term storage unless explicitly flagged for debugging.
   - Observability export: telemetry exporter streams sampled traces/tokens to an observability cluster that enforces token redaction before indexing. Sampling is workload-driven and can be disabled.

2) Credentialing / Access controls:
   - Operator access: SSO (OIDC) + MFA required. Role-based access with least privilege policies. Elevated actions (key unwrap, debug dumps) require JIT approval and two-person approval for production scopes.
   - Service identities: short-lived certs and ephemeral tokens for pods issued via our workload identity system; pod tokens do not grant direct KMS access.
   - KMS: Customer-managed keys supported via external KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Default (hosted) customers use Redwood-managed KMS; key access audited and requires operator justification.

3) Subprocessors and compliance:
   - Current roster: metrics provider (Metricly Inc. — SOC2 Type II), object storage (CloudStore — SOC2 Type II), SSO provider (AuthScale — SOC2), infra provider (CloudAero — ISO27001). Detailed roster and certification dates are in the attached doc.

4) Retention windows and deletion:
   - Token-level telemetry: default 30 days, configurable by contract; can be truncated to 0 for strict controls.
   - Aggregates/metrics: 24 months.
   - Audit logs: default 12 months; extended retention add-on available.

5) Cross-border controls:
   - Region pinning and egress gating supported. Transfers documented in the DPA transfer annex; subprocessors aligned to region-specific endpoints. We will provide the annex with SCC references for EU transfers.

Attachments and artifacts packaged: redwood_dataflow_v2.svg (diagram), ssq_response_draft.docx (detailed Q&A), subprocessors_roster.csv (compliance snapshot).

- Legal teams: once we agree, Dylan will prepare the DPA annex language and we can circulate DocuSign.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
